title: Admissibility-blocked claim text is handed verbatim to the persona voice call
description: turn.py:148 _voice_prompt() interpolates turn_log.reason straight into the persona prompt. When moves.choose_move downgrades a reveal to abstain, admissibility._grounded() puts the blocked entry's full claim TEXT inside each 'missing' element (admissibility.py:62 for assumed, :67 for unsupported inferred_by_model), and moves.py builds the reason as 'conclusion blocked by admissibility check; missing: <claim text>'. So the exact sentence the checker just refused to let the bot state is shipped into the user-facing call, at the persona's own widened temperature, under the instruction 'just speak'. The voice call sees no ledger and no board, so this reason string is the ONLY channel by which producer-side content reaches the speaking model -- the blocked claim is not incidental context, it is essentially the whole prompt, which makes paraphrasing it the model's most available continuation. Meanwhile turn_log.move still reads 'abstain', so the audit record says the bot held back on a turn where it did not. Every blocked entry contributes its claim text, so the leak grows with the ungrounded chain. This is the narrator-cby.4.1 shape and it contradicts moves.py's own stated invariant that 'there is no route from I have a conclusion to I said it out loud that skips the check' -- the route exists, it runs through the reason string. Reproduced end to end through ChatCore.observe + run_turn during the 2026-09-03 adversarial sweep of narrator-9nl.
acceptance_criteria: The voice prompt for an admissibility-blocked turn carries no claim text from a blocked ledger entry -- pass the missing entry IDS or a claim-free summary, keeping the full missing tuple on the TurnLog where the audit record wants it. A turn.py self-check asserts a blocked entry's claim string does not appear in the voice call's prompt, using the same leak-check technique chapters.py uses for sim.culprit.
close_reason: Closed at both ends. (1) admissibility._grounded() no longer quotes entry.claim into the missing tuple -- it names ids and why each leg failed. The ledger already holds the claim under that id, and every existing consumer (moves.py, chat_core.py, panel.py, admissibility's own self-check) asserts on ids, never on claim text, so nothing was lost; what went away is a checker copying the exact content it just refused into a string downstream code renders. (2) turn._voice_prompt() is now an explicit trust boundary: a checker-downgraded abstain (move==ABSTAIN and missing non-empty, which a directly-requested abstain never is) gets a fixed _BLOCKED_VOICE_REASON instead of turn_log.reason. TurnLog.missing and TurnLog.reason are unchanged, so the audit record keeps everything. Leak reproduced against the pre-fix tree (the refused sentence appeared verbatim in the voice prompt while turn_log.move read abstain) and confirmed gone after. Self-checks: turn.py runs the chapters.py-style leak check on the actual emitted prompt over a blocked reveal, a plain abstain (keeps its own reason), and an admissible reveal (still reaches the voice); admissibility.py asserts across three blocked shapes that missing names the failing leg and carries no claim text. Nine mutations killed, including boundary-removed, boundary-always-fires, boundary-keyed-on-move-alone, boundary-swallows-an-allowed-reveal, and re-adding the claim quote in either admissibility branch -- that last one is caught by turn.py's check as well as admissibility's, so the two ends cover each other. moves.py's docstring records why its 'no route that skips the check' claim needed the repair.

title: Mode flag: simulation and product read the sweep opposite ways
description: C3 is labelled a pathology simulation and its whole payload is watching personality distort group reasoning. Flooring agreeableness there deletes the phenomenon the harness exists to show. C5 has a human inside the system rather than observing it, where a bot that defers to a bad claim is a liability and the person harmed is the one least able to see it happening. Same machinery, opposite success criteria, so make the mode explicit rather than implied by which module imported it.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation mode lets the persona act on its weights unimpeded and records the damage. Product mode acts on the log and withholds. Constructing without a mode raises rather than defaulting.
close_reason: TraitMode(SIMULATION|PRODUCT) added to trait_evidence.py, wired into turn.py's run_turn (required keyword-only trait_mode, no default) and metrics.py's chat_record; self-checks cover raise-on-missing/invalid mode, PRODUCT byte-identical to pre-.3.10 behavior, and SIMULATION overriding both reveal-shaped trait gaps with Damage records while narrator-7gj leak boundary holds. Full module sweep + pytest pass.

title: Traits move evidence weights; log the counterfactual when it bites
description: Agreeable people genuinely weight testimony from people they like more heavily. That is an evidence effect, not a tone effect, and a ledger that scores all testimony identically has amputated something real. So traits reach the weights: openness sets how many hypotheses stay live, conscientiousness sets the evidence bar for reveal, agreeableness weights source credibility and governs concession. No clamping. Instead, when the persona would have taken a move that admissibility refuses, log both: what the trait wanted, what the ledger licensed, and the gap. The distinction being modelled is public compliance versus private acceptance. Agreeableness loads hard on the public side, so it fully governs the reply while the ledger records the private read that moved less.
acceptance_criteria: A withheld concession appears in the transcript with the trait value, the move the persona selected, and the missing evidence named. Nothing is suppressed without a corresponding log line.
close_reason: trait_evidence.py built + wired into turn.py/metrics.py; withheld-concession gap appears in chat_session.jsonl turn 4 with trait value, selected move, and missing evidence named; all module self-checks + pytest pass. Handoff at sandbox-handoffs/narrator-c5b.3.9.md

title: Two-channel turn: persona-neutral reasoning, persona voice
description: Split each turn into two model calls. The reasoning pass updates the ledger and the board, runs the admissibility check and picks a move, at a low fixed temperature. The voice pass renders the chosen move in character using the compiled Ocean sampler. The failure this prevents is neuroticism widening temperature on the step that decides what is true. Note the scope limit: this separates sampler settings from reasoning, not traits from evidence. Trait effects on evidence weighting are P2's problem and are deliberately not solved here.
acceptance_criteria: Sampler settings from a profile reach the voice call only. A single-pass mode stays available so a learner can watch the difference.
close_reason: Built turn.py: two-channel run_turn() with TWO_PASS (persona-neutral REASONING_PROFILE for the decision call, real persona for voice) and SINGLE_PASS (persona drives both). Self-check verifies reasoning-call options stay identical across different personas while voice-call options track the persona, and asserts the single-pass contrast the AC asks for. All self-checks + pytest pass.

title: Invert validate_solvability() into a runtime admissibility check
description: narrator-cby.7 built the epistemic clue graph and solvability check for generated mysteries: given the clues, does exactly one suspect survive. Turn it around. Given the ledger, is the conclusion the bot is about to state derivable from entries the user has seen. If not, the conclusion is inadmissible and the bot names the evidence it would need. Fair play as a runtime guard.
acceptance_criteria: A conclusion resting on an inferred-only chain is blocked and reported. The check runs on the ledger, with no access to the generator's ground truth.
notes: Implemented in admissibility.py (check(), Verdict) as part of the narrator-c5b.3 session. Recursive grounding over ledger entries only, no ground-truth access. Self-check: uv run python admissibility.py -> ok. Full writeup: sandbox-handoffs/narrator-c5b.3.md
close_reason: Admissibility check implemented (admissibility.py), inverted from mystery.validate_solvability(); AC verified by self-check. See sandbox-handoffs/narrator-c5b.3.md

title: Hypothesis board over live interpretations
description: Hold three to five readings of what the user wants, each with a weight, updated as evidence arrives. Premature collapse onto the first plausible reading is the single thing that makes a chatbot feel stupid, and the genre's engine is that the obvious suspect is wrong. Board is dumped on demand so a learner can watch weights move.
acceptance_criteria: A conversation that reverses direction shows the weight shift in the dump rather than a silent switch. Collapsing below two live hypotheses requires evidence that rules the others out.
close_reason: Implemented hypothesis_board.py: HypothesisBoard with reweight()/rule_out()/dump(), self-check demonstrates a reversal on record in history and enforces rule_out (with reason) as the only path below the live-hypothesis floor. uv run pytest passes.

Four structures: an evidence ledger with provenance, a board of live interpretations, an admissibility check inverted from validate_solvability(), and an explicit move set. Same abstention spine as mathgraph and certabstain.

title: Evidence ledger with provenance tags
description: One append-only JSONL ledger per conversation. Each entry carries a claim, the turn it entered on, and a provenance tag: stated by the user, observed in an artifact, inferred by the model, or assumed. The distinction is the whole point, since testimony and deduction are not the same evidence and most chatbots blur them. Flush per line and reuse the file:line error context from load_transcript.
acceptance_criteria: A ledger survives a run killed mid-write and reads back with the offending line named. Every entry has a provenance tag; untagged entries are rejected at write time.
notes: Implemented in evidence_ledger.py (EvidenceLedger, load()) as part of the narrator-c5b.3 session. Provenance checked at write time; mid-write-kill read-back names file:line via load(), mirroring agents.load_transcript. Self-check: uv run python evidence_ledger.py -> ok. Full writeup: sandbox-handoffs/narrator-c5b.3.md
close_reason: Evidence ledger with provenance tags implemented (evidence_ledger.py); AC verified by self-check. See sandbox-handoffs/narrator-c5b.3.md

title: C5: Narrator as a fair-play chatbot
description: Turn the mystery engine around and point it at the conversation. mystery.py holds ground truth in WorldSimulation and checks with validate_solvability() that the clues reach the culprit. In chat the user holds ground truth and the bot deduces, so solvability becomes a runtime constraint on the bot: it may assert only what is derivable from evidence the user has actually seen. That is the Knox/Van Dine fair-play rule as a hallucination guard, and the same untrusted-producer/independent-checker split as certkit.
acceptance_criteria: A learner can hold a conversation, read the ledger and hypothesis board it produced, and point at the specific entry that licensed each conclusion. Every turn logs which move was chosen and why.

title: Reverse the 'local Ollama only' non-goal, on the record
description: prd.md lists 'No cloud model providers. Local Ollama only.' under Non-goals. Adding a Fable backend reverses that, for an audience of three teenagers. The change is real: API keys, per-token cost, network dependency, and their text leaving the machine. Record the decision and its scope before any backend code lands, and amend prd.md in the same change.
acceptance_criteria: prd.md no longer claims a non-goal the code contradicts. The decision states what stays local by default, what the cloud path is for, and who holds the key.
close_reason: prd.md non-goal amended in the same change; decision records what stays local by default (Ollama, all existing entry points), what the cloud path is for (opt-in Fable per learner, see .2.2/.2.5), and who holds the key (learner, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from env only, name-the-missing-var on failure). uv run pytest passes.

title: Discussion protocol and the unshared-clue measure
description: Run agents.converse over the partition and record, per clue, whether it was ever voiced, by whom, on which turn, and whether anyone built on it after. The classic finding is that shared information is mentioned earlier and repeated more while unique information stays unvoiced or gets dropped after one mention, so mention count alone is the wrong measure and uptake has to be tracked separately. Add the group's final answer and whether it matches the culprit.
acceptance_criteria: Per-clue voiced, uptake and turn-first-mentioned columns come out of a run. Group answer is scored against ground truth the agents never saw.
close_reason: Implemented discussion.py: run_discussion() runs agents.converse() over a clue_partition split (each agent's Agent.evidence is exactly their partition.agent_clues(i), never the pooled set or sim.culprit), producing clue_report() (per-clue shared/unique, voiced, first_speaker, first_turn, mention_count, uptake) and final_answer() (group's answer read from the transcript, scored against sim.culprit only after the fact as culprit_hit). agents.py got a one-field extension (Agent.evidence) to carry private per-agent context through the existing converse() loop, backward-compatible (default empty string, existing self-check unchanged plus one new pinning assertion). Verified via python discussion.py -> ok, python agents.py -> ok, and uv run pytest. Handoff at sandbox-handoffs/narrator-cby.3.5.2.md.

title: Clue partitioner with a solvability contract
description: Split the clue set across N agents such that the union satisfies validate_solvability() and every individual subset does not. Shared clues go to everyone, unique clues to exactly one agent. The partition is the experimental manipulation, so it needs to be seeded, recorded, and reproducible. Reject a partition that fails either half of the contract rather than running a degenerate condition and reporting it as a result.
acceptance_criteria: Union is solvable, every subset is not, both checked by the existing validator rather than by construction. Rejected partitions name which half failed. Same seed reproduces the same split.
close_reason: Implemented clue_partition.py: partition() splits an EpistemicClueGraph's clues across N agents (seeded, reproducible), checks both halves of the contract via the real mystery.EpistemicClueGraph.validate_solvability() (never reimplemented), and raises PartitionError naming which half failed. Self-check exercises union-half and individual-half rejection separately, plus a solvable normal split. Verified via python clue_partition.py -> ok, a manual 18-combination seed/agent-count sweep, and pytest. Handoff at sandbox-handoffs/narrator-cby.3.5.1.md.

title: Hidden-profile harness over the mystery generator
description: Stasser and Titus's paradigm: distribute information so no individual can reach the right answer alone but the pooled set can, then watch groups spend their discussion on what everyone already knew and miss the solution. The effect is robust in meta-analysis and it is isomorphic to what mystery.py already builds. The generator holds ground truth, the clue graph knows which clues are load-bearing, and validate_solvability() already answers whether a clue set narrows to one suspect. Partition that set across agents instead of handing it to one solver and C3 becomes an experiment with a correct answer rather than a transcript with vibes. The pathology it exposes is the one metrics.py already counts.
acceptance_criteria: A run reports whether the group reached the culprit, which clues were never voiced, and which agent held them. Ground truth stays out of every agent's context.
close_reason: Parent AC already satisfied by closed children .3.5.1 (clue_partition.py) and .3.5.2 (discussion.py): a run reports culprit_hit, per-clue voiced/held_by via clue_report(), and ground truth (sim.culprit) never enters any Agent's evidence or the partitioner. Re-verified this session (not trusted from the prior close text): uv run python on mystery.py/clue_partition.py/discussion.py/agents.py/metrics.py all print ok, a live --seed run reaches the model boundary and fails only on absent local Ollama (no live server in sandbox), uv run pytest passes. .3.5.3 (trait/role conditions) and .3.5.4 (pooling metrics in metrics.py) are real follow-on scope, already filed as children with their own AC, and stay open -- neither is required by this parent's stated AC. Handoff at sandbox-handoffs/narrator-cby.3.5.md.

title: rule_out() renormalizes surviving weights with no BoardEvent, desyncing history from the board
description: After retiring a hypothesis, hypothesis_board.rule_out() (around line 122) divides every survivor's weight by the remaining total and appends nothing to history; the only event written is the rule_out for the retired id. dump()['history'] therefore stops reconstructing dump()['hypotheses'], contradicting the module docstring's first rule ('Every weight change is appended to history, never just applied in place') and dump()'s own promise that the board never 'quietly points somewhere else than it used to'. Unlike the extreme-value defects filed alongside it, this is UNCONDITIONAL -- it fires on every rule_out with ordinary weights. Reproduced twice on 2026-09-03, once standalone and once on the live ChatCore.conclude() path: replaying the record yielded a board summing to 0.9 while the real board summed to 1.0. Magnitude is unbounded -- retiring a hypothesis holding 0.9 of the mass moved a survivor from 0.05 to 0.50, from last place to board leader, with zero history entries attributing the move to anything. The board's own arithmetic is right; only the recording is missing. In a repo whose claim is that a conclusion follows from evidence checked independently, the audit record is exactly the artifact a learner is supposed to be able to trust. Fix is one appended reweight-kind BoardEvent per survivor inside the renormalization loop (reason e.g. 'renormalized after ruling out <id>'), mirroring what reweight() already does at lines 92-97.
acceptance_criteria: A hypothesis_board.py self-check that replays dump()['history'] from the initial uniform prior and asserts the reconstructed weights equal dump()['hypotheses'] exactly, after a rule_out -- not just after a reweight.
close_reason: rule_out() now appends a reweight-kind BoardEvent per survivor whose weight the renormalization actually moved, attributed to the elimination that caused it ('renormalized after ruling out <id>'), mirroring what reweight() already did. Verified pre/post: on a board reweighted to a=0.9/b=0.05/c=0.05 then ruling out a, the pre-fix history replayed to {a:0.0, b:0.05, c:0.05} summing to 0.1 while the board held {a:0.0, b:0.5, c:0.5} summing to 1.0 -- b went from last place to leader with nothing in the record attributing the move. Post-fix the two agree exactly. Self-check adds a replay() that rebuilds the board from the uniform prior and its own history and asserts exact equality of weight and liveness, cross-checking each event's old_weight against the replayed state first so a gap surfaces at the next event on that hypothesis rather than absorbing into the total; it runs over the full existing scenario (2 reweights, 3 eliminations, collapse to one survivor) and over a fresh board where the elimination visibly re-orders the survivors. SCOPE EXTENSION, flagged deliberately: reweight() had the identical hole one line over -- its 'abs(new - old) > 1e-12' guard applied a change and skipped recording it -- so the invariant would still have been false after fixing rule_out alone. Changed to 'new != old', with a self-check case that moves every weight by ~1.1e-13 (a real change the old guard dropped) and one asserting a no-op reweight still writes nothing. chat_core.py's assertion that history[-1] is the rule_out was updated to find the rule_out rather than assume the board stopped moving when it fired; it now also asserts the entries after it name that rule_out. Six of seven mutations killed. The one survivor is rule_out's 'if total > 0' guard, which only matters on a board whose weights have already collapsed to zero -- that state is narrator-7z7's, and its acceptance criteria makes it unreachable, so it is not covered here rather than being covered badly.

title: select_question()'s honest abstention becomes a persona-invented, unscored question
description: turn.py run_turn (lines 223-229) sets ask_text only when question_log.chosen is not None, and _voice_prompt drops the ask clause when ask_text is falsy -- but the surrounding sentence 'The reasoning channel chose to ask this turn... Write the reply in character' is emitted unconditionally. So on an honest abstention the voice call is told to ask with no question supplied, at the persona's own trait-derived sampler settings, and whatever it invents becomes out.reply while question_log records chosen=None with every candidate discriminates=False. The transcript then contains a question that was neither scored nor selected, and the audit trail cannot reconstruct what the bot asked or why. This inverts turn.py's own docstring ('select_question()'s winner, not the model's free-form invention, is what the voice call is told to ask') and question_selector's ('not a silent fallback to asking whatever came first in the list') -- it is worse than the first candidate, it is a candidate that never existed. Not an edge case: once the board narrows to ONE live hypothesis, _spread() is 1 - 1.0**2 == 0.0 for every possible candidate, so chosen is None by construction and every subsequent ask turn takes the invent-your-own path -- exactly the endgame state a mystery converges to. The existing self-check at turn.py:406 only asserts the negative ('specific question' not in prompt), certifying the clause is absent without noticing the ask instruction remains. Reproduced 2026-09-03.
acceptance_criteria: When the move is ask and no question was selected, run_turn does not instruct the voice to ask -- it renders the turn as an abstain-shaped 'nothing worth asking' reply, or states that no question was chosen. A turn.py self-check asserts the voice prompt for a chosen=None ask turn contains no instruction to ask a question, and covers the single-live-hypothesis endgame explicitly.
close_reason: run_turn now downgrades a declined ask to abstain, the same shape moves.choose_move already applies to a reveal admissibility.check() refuses: select_question is the checker for ask, so an ask it declined lands as abstain with a reason saying why (_no_question_worth_asking). Previously the voice call was told 'you chose to ask' with no question attached and the persona invented one -- both the generic turn-burning question question_selector.py's docstring opens by condemning, and a reply the SelectionLog could not account for. The downgraded TurnLog leaves missing empty, which is what narrator-7gj's blocked-reveal boundary keys on, so the two abstain shapes stay distinguishable in the log and the declined ask keeps its own reason. question_log is still returned on a downgraded turn -- every candidate stays scored and logged, which is what makes 'nothing was worth asking' auditable rather than asserted. Verified pre/post against HEAD on the endgame path (board at one live hypothesis: pre-fix logged move=ask and told the voice to ask with chosen=None; post-fix logs abstain and the voice is not told to ask). Self-check covers the declined-ask turn (move, reason, empty missing, rejected candidate's text absent from the voice prompt, full scored log retained) and the single-live-hypothesis endgame explicitly, where every candidate scores 0 by construction. Six mutations killed: downgrade removed, downgrade always fires, downgrade keeps move=ask, downgrade populates missing, downgraded log built but discarded, and TurnOutput reporting the pre-downgrade log. Known ceiling recorded as a ponytail comment: with one live hypothesis every ask lands here, and if the endgame should still ask confirming questions the fix belongs in question_selector (a reason to ask beyond discrimination), not a special case in turn.py.

title: parse_candidates() is a half-implemented trust boundary: only predicted_answers completeness is validated
description: question_selector.parse_candidates() docstring claims it exists so 'a malformed or lazy model response is a named ValueError at the source, not a KeyError raised later, deep inside select_question'. It validates one field and lets three other malformed shapes through, all reproduced end to end through turn.run_turn during the 2026-09-03 sweep: (1) UNHASHABLE VALUES -- it checks only that the KEYS of predicted_answers cover every live hypothesis, never that the VALUES are hashable, so a model hedging with a JSON array ('blackwood': ['study','library']) parses fine and dies with TypeError: unhashable type: 'list' at _spread's group accumulator (question_selector.py:87). Aborts the whole turn: no reply, no log, no abstention. (2) DUPLICATE IDS -- nothing rejects a repeated candidate id, and turn.py:227 recovers the winner with next(s.text for s in scored if s.id == chosen), which stops on the FIRST match. A generator emitting generic ids like q1/q2 (candidate_prompt asks for '<short id>' with no uniqueness instruction) makes the bot SPEAK a question the scorer marked discriminates=False while the SelectionLog reports a winner at score 0.75 -- a silently-wrong audit log, and exactly what the module docstring says cannot happen ('rejected outright rather than merely scored low, so a caller can never accidentally spend a turn on it'). A winner with empty text is the same three lines: ask_text is falsy, turn.py:146 drops the ask clause, and the voice call is told nothing while chosen still names a winner. (3) MISSING KEYS -- it hard-indexes c['id'] and c['text'] at line 201 and calls c.get() at 195, so drifted key names raise KeyError('id') and a list of bare strings raises AttributeError, both escaping run_turn uncaught. Root cause is one function: parse_candidates is where every caller's model output becomes Candidates. evidence_ledger.py:62 and hypothesis_board.py:61 already reject duplicate ids for their own ids.
acceptance_criteria: parse_candidates() raises a named ValueError for: a non-hashable predicted-answer value, a repeated candidate id, a missing id/text key, and a non-dict candidate entry. score_candidate() also guards the unhashable case directly, since select_question() is callable with hand-built Candidates that never went through parse. turn.py either carries the winning ScoredCandidate instead of re-looking-up its id, or the duplicate-id guard makes the lookup safe. Self-check cases for each, and a turn.py case asserting a rejected candidate's text never reaches the voice prompt.
close_reason: parse_candidates() now validates every shape it used to let through, each as a named ValueError naming the generator: a non-object candidate entry (was AttributeError on .get), a missing/blank/non-string id or text (was KeyError('id')), a repeated candidate id, a non-object predicted_answers, the existing completeness rule, and a non-hashable predicted answer (was TypeError: unhashable type: 'list' from _spread's group accumulator, aborting the whole turn with no reply and no abstention). The hashability rule lives in one shared _as_group_key() used by both parse_candidates and _spread, so select_question() is guarded too when handed hand-built Candidates that never passed through parse -- the acceptance criteria's second half. select_question() also enforces id uniqueness itself, because its own return value is a bare id and cannot name one of two candidates sharing it. candidate_prompt() now states the uniqueness rule to the generator rather than only punishing its absence. Verified pre/post through run_turn on the duplicate-id case, which was the silent one rather than a crash: pre-fix the SelectionLog reported chosen='q1' scoring 0.67 while the voice call was handed the OTHER q1, the uniform candidate the scorer had marked discriminates=False at score 0.00 -- the bot asked a question the checker rejected while its audit record named the one it picked. Post-fix it is rejected at the boundary. Self-checks cover all eight rejections plus both hand-built routes into select_question, and turn.py asserts four drift shapes propagate out of run_turn as named ValueErrors. Eight mutations run, eight killed; the kill messages reproduce the original defects verbatim (TypeError: unhashable type: 'list', KeyError: 'id', AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get').

title: Agreeableness sweep, scored in both directions
description: Sweep agreeableness from -1 to +1 through the C3 scarce-resource scenario and score the same run under both readings. In simulation mode, admissibility failures must track the trait: if they stay flat, the trait is not reaching anything that matters and the simulation is decorative. In product mode, concession rate must move while withheld conclusions stay clean: if a bad claim survives to the reply, the counterfactual log failed to catch it. One sweep, two assertions, opposite signs.

title: Explicit move set: reveal, complicate, ask, abstain
description: Each turn picks a move before it picks words. Most chatbots only ever have reveal, and mystery structure is mostly about what you hold back. Log the chosen move and the reason next to the reply, which is the observable output the PRD requires of every component.
acceptance_criteria: Every logged turn carries a move and a reason. A turn whose conclusion fails admissibility cannot choose reveal.

title: Discriminating-question selector
description: Instead of a generic clarifying question, score candidates by how differently the live hypotheses predict the answer and ask the one with the widest spread. Columbo's one-more-thing: boring under every hypothesis except one. Cap at one question per turn. Anthropic's persona-vector work found that responses to underspecified queries push toward hallucination, so failing to ask is itself an error source rather than merely a missed opportunity.
acceptance_criteria: Given a board, the selector prefers the question that splits it and rejects questions every hypothesis answers the same way. Selection scores are logged.
close_reason: Built question_selector.py: score_candidate() (weighted Gini impurity over live-hypothesis board weight) + select_question() (picks highest-scoring discriminating candidate, or None if nothing splits the board; logs every candidate's score in SelectionLog). Self-check demonstrates preference for the widest-spread question over a Columbo-shaped 3-vs-1 split and a uniform 'boring' question (score 0.0, rejected), plus a reweighted-board scenario showing the selector reads current board weight, not just live-id count. uv run pytest passes; all C5 module self-checks re-verified. acceptance_criteria: A run that would exceed the ceiling stops with the count and the limit named. prd.md says which components default to which backend.
close_reason: agents.converse() now takes token_budget (default DEFAULT_TOKEN_BUDGET=20_000), estimates tokens with a stdlib len//4 heuristic, and raises TokenBudgetExceeded naming the turn, projected count, and limit before spending past it; token_budget=None opts out. prd.md's forward-reference to this bead is replaced with the actual cost breakdown per component (linear/bounded vs agents.converse's quadratic growth). title: Record which evidence answered which question, so 'did the question split the board' becomes measurable
description: narrator-c5b.3.7 had to drop the measure the bead literally asked for -- how often a chosen question actually split the board -- because it is not recoverable from the chat log. The board narrows only via HypothesisBoard.rule_out, which chat_core.conclude calls only on a reveal that passed admissibility, while turn.run_turn populates question_log only when the move is ask. Nothing ties a reveal's citations back to a question asked earlier, so any 'the board narrowed after the question' number is really measuring whether the next turn happened to be a successful reveal, on evidence that may predate the question entirely. It is also capped at (live-1) landings per conversation regardless of question quality, so a longer conversation with better questions scores lower. metrics.py ships the honest substitutes instead: question yield (how often the selector found something worth asking) and answer rate (whether new stated_by_user evidence arrived on the following turn). What would make the real measure possible: have the turn loop stamp evidence observed in response to a question with the question id that prompted it, so a later reveal's citation chain can be traced back to the question that elicited it. That is the same bookkeeping narrator-c5b.3.6's Chekhov ledger needs, so it likely belongs there rather than in a separate mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: A chat log carries, for each ledger entry, the id of the question that prompted it (or None). metrics.py reports how often a chosen question's elicited evidence appears in the citation chain of a later landed reveal, and a self-check covers a question whose answer grounds a reveal and one whose answer never gets used.
close_reason: Implementation was already complete in the uncommitted working tree from a prior unfinished session (prompted_by on LedgerEntry, question_selector.question_id, ChatCore.observe wiring, metrics.question_grounding with chat_metrics/chat_summary integration). Verified against acceptance criteria clause-by-clause, fixed a stale docstring reference, re-ran full self-check sweep + pytest, all green. Handoff at sandbox-handoffs/narrator-5ob.md.

title: turn.py's ask-path self-check cannot tell select_question()'s winner from the first candidate
description: SelectionLog.scored is explicitly 'in input order' (question_selector.py:64) while chosen is max(winners, key=score), so scored[0] and the winner are genuinely different things. But turn.py's _self_check() fixture lists the discriminating candidate 'whereabouts' FIRST, so in the only ask turn where chosen is not None, winner == scored[0]. Mutating turn.py:227 from 'next(s.text for s in question_log.scored if s.id == question_log.chosen)' to 'question_log.scored[0].text' still prints ok -- verified 2026-09-03 -- and tests/ holds nothing but assert True. The single assertion 'Where were you at the time of the murder?' in voice_call.prompt is therefore vacuous with respect to the property it is written to defend: the chatbot would burn every ask turn on whichever question the generator emitted first while TurnOutput.question_log kept reporting the correctly-scored winner. In this repo's vocabulary that is the producer (the model's candidate ordering) silently overriding the checker (Gini scoring), with a silently-wrong log and no test noticing. The second ask turn does not cover it either, because the 'if question_log.chosen is not None' guard leaves that path unchanged. Shipped behavior today is correct -- this is a missing regression guard, not a live wrong answer.
acceptance_criteria: turn.py's ask-path fixture lists the uninformative candidate BEFORE the discriminating one, and asserts both that the winner's text reaches the voice prompt and that the loser's text does not. Mutating the winner lookup to scored[0] must make the self-check fail.
close_reason: turn.py's ask-path fixture now makes the winner unreachable by any positional or first-match shortcut. It listed the discriminating candidate first, so scored[0] == chosen and 'ask_text = question_log.scored[0].text' passed the entire self-check. Reordering alone was not enough -- that just moved the coincidence to scored[-1], which survived the first mutation round. The fixture is now four candidates: uniform 'boring', a weak 3-vs-1 discriminator 'weak' (0.375), the clean 4-way winner 'whereabouts' (0.75) third, and uniform 'weather' last. The winner is at neither end and is not the first candidate that discriminates. Assertions pin the input order, assert weak.discriminates and weak.score < whereabouts.score so the fixture cannot silently degrade, and check that none of the three rejected candidates' texts reach the voice prompt. Four mutations killed: scored[0], scored[-1], first-that-discriminates, and min-instead-of-max.

title: reweight() validates its inputs but never its results: weights reach exactly 0.0 or nan
description: hypothesis_board.reweight() validates each SUPPLIED weight with 'w <= 0' but never constrains the RESULT raw[hid]/total. Three finite, strictly-positive weights (1e308 each) sum to inf and every live hypothesis lands on weight exactly 0.0 while live stays True -- the precise opposite of the docstring ('can push a hypothesis arbitrarily close to zero but never to it -- driving it out entirely is rule_out's job') and of the guard whose own error message says 'rule it out with evidence instead'. The board is then permanently broken through the public API: rule_out's 'if total > 0' guard sees 0.0 and skips renormalization, leaving survivors live at 0.0; the next reweight raises ZeroDivisionError; and question_selector.select_question raises ZeroDivisionError inside _spread. An inf input -- which passes 'w <= 0', and which json.loads('1e400') produces from a model emitting 1e999 -- writes nan into a live hypothesis with NO history entry at all, because abs(nan - old) > 1e-12 is False: a weight change applied in place with no record, the one thing the module docstring says cannot happen. A nan board also makes question_selector's scorer emit an affirmatively false audit reason, describing a clean three-way split as belief that is 'already all but ruled out'. Trigger is pathological (weights spanning >300 orders of magnitude, or a literal inf) and reweight has no production caller today -- grep finds it only in self-checks -- hence P3. Reproduced 2026-09-03. Fix is one line: reject a non-finite or non-positive total, or validate the quotient the way the input is validated.
acceptance_criteria: reweight() raises on a non-finite supplied weight and on a total that is not finite and positive; a self-check covers the 1e308-overflow and inf cases and asserts no live hypothesis ends at weight 0.0 or nan.
close_reason: reweight() now validates results, not just inputs. isfinite() is checked before the zero guard because nan <= 0 is False and a nan walked straight through; the normalization total must be finite and positive; and every resulting quotient must be finite and > 0, so a hypothesis can no longer be retired by arithmetic. Everything is validated before anything is written, so a rejected reweight leaves the board and its history exactly as it found them -- asserted in every rejection case, including one where the failing hypothesis is the second checked, which is what makes that assertion do real work. Verified pre/post against HEAD: 1e308 x3 previously left every live hypothesis at 0.0 (and select_question then raised ZeroDivisionError inside _spread), an inf weight left one at nan and the rest at 0.0, and 1e-320 alongside 1e300 retired a live hypothesis to exactly 0.0 -- all three now rejected with named errors. FOLLOW-ON, in scope: rule_out's 'if total > 0:' branch existed only to cope with the collapsed board this bead makes impossible, and its way of coping was to skip renormalization, leaving survivors at 0.0 and the board silently broken. It is now unreachable -- reweight refuses any non-positive result and a float sum is never smaller than its largest addend -- so the branch is gone; a loud ZeroDivisionError would beat a quiet wrong board if it ever became reachable again. That closes the one mutation left uncovered when narrator-eeb was closed. Six mutations killed, including a re-check that eeb's survivor-renormalization events are still recorded. All 16 module self-checks and pytest pass, and the C4 partition parity harness (25 seeds x every clue subset) is still byte-identical.

title: validate_solvability()'s could_have_left_trace reads the culprit's own trajectory
description: mystery.EpistemicClueGraph.validate_solvability() -> suspects_consistent_with_clues() -> could_have_left_trace() reads sim.trajectories[sim.culprit][last] for the flee room. That is a ground-truth value not present in the clue subgraph the checker is supposed to be limited to -- a producer/checker discipline smell in the one function that is supposed to embody the discipline. Currently INERT: the flee room is hardcoded 'Library' (mystery.py:~67) and the crime scene 'Study', so can_reach('Study','Library',1) is always True and could_have_left_trace collapses to pure geometry; the footprint clue also publicly encodes that room, so the value is observable anyway. But it is a latent path for the check to consult the answer, and it would bite the moment the flee room becomes seed-dependent. Surfaced by the 2026-08-30 vetting pass; pre-existing, not introduced by the hidden-profile harness work. Fix: pass the flee room in as a clue-derived value (it is already in the footprint clue), or take it from the subgraph, so could_have_left_trace() never dereferences sim.culprit.
acceptance_criteria: could_have_left_trace() (and anything validate_solvability transitively calls) provably reads no sim.culprit / sim.trajectories value; a self-check or comment documents that the flee room now comes from the clue set. Existing mystery.py self-check and validate_solvability seed sweep stay green.
notes: Follow-up during the same session: the first version of this fix raised ValueError when the clue set held no trace clue, which broke clue_partition.py and discussion.py -- the hidden-profile harness hands the checker arbitrary clue subsets via _subgraph_view, and a subset without Clue_Footprint is normal. _flee_room_from_clues() now returns None there and could_have_left_trace() treats None as 'no flight to place', falling back to opportunity alone. That is exactly what the pre-fix code did on such a subset (it read the real flee room off ground truth and can_reach(crime_scene, flee_room, 1) was True), and it was verified rather than assumed: a parity harness comparing pre-fix and post-fix output over 25 seeds x every subset of the clue nodes (2^n per seed) -- solver answers, validate_solvability verdicts, and 2- and 3-agent partition assignments -- is byte-identical. Returning False there instead would alibi every holder of an alibi clue and let a solo agent who never saw the footprint 'solve' the case, collapsing the hidden-profile contract; there is now a self-check assertion against that. Also strengthened the proof: an alibi clue always fails had_opportunity, so the checker short-circuits before the can_reach branch and a ground-truth read hiding there ran under no guard -- the self-check now calls could_have_left_trace directly through the blindfolded engine with a room that does have opportunity. Five mutations killed in total.
close_reason: could_have_left_trace() now takes flee_room as a parameter and no longer dereferences sim.trajectories[sim.culprit]; suspects_consistent_with_clues() supplies it from the published Clue_Footprint node via a new _flee_room_from_clues(), so the solver reads the clue set it is meant to be limited to. exonerating_sighting() still reads trajectories and correctly so -- it is only ever called from build_clues(), on the producer's side; the rule is 'the checker never touches ground truth', not 'nothing does', and that contrast is now documented on the class. PROOF TECHNIQUE, worth recording: an output-equivalence test cannot verify this fix. The leak was inert exactly as the bead said -- can_reach(crime_scene, flee_room, 1) is the same constant for every alibi clue, so it factors out of the comparison. Confirmed empirically against the pre-fix code: moving the culprit's flee room to Kitchen, Foyer or Hallway across seeds 3, 7 and 11 left the solver's answer unchanged every time, so a move-ground-truth-and-check-the-answer test would have passed against the broken code. The self-check therefore proves it by denial of access: a _NoGroundTruth proxy wraps the sim and raises on culprit/trajectories/causal, and the solver is run through it over 20 seeds, still landing on the culprit. Three mutations killed: restoring the original leak and pointing _flee_room_from_clues at the sim both trip the guard with 'the solver reached for ground truth: sim.trajectories'; disarming the guard itself is caught by an explicit assertion that FORBIDDEN is non-empty (added after that mutation initially survived -- the loop testing the guard was vacuous with an empty tuple, the same vacuous-assertion shape narrator-euj is filed for).

title: question_selector.score_candidate() crashes on near-zero hypothesis weights
description: question_selector.score_candidate() does `(only_answer,) = groups.keys()` in its not-discriminates branch, assuming exactly one predicted-answer group. But _spread() returns a value <= _EPS (1e-9) whenever the minority mass fraction is below ~5e-10 even though two or more distinct predicted answers exist, so the unpack raises ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1). Reproduced from the public API: HypothesisBoard.reweight(1, {'a':1.0,'b':1.0,'c':1e-12}, 'x') (reweight rejects only w<=0, not tiny positives), then select_question(board, n, [Candidate('q','',{'a':'no','b':'no','c':'yes'})]) raises instead of returning a SelectionLog. Needs a pathologically lopsided board, not normal operation -- all self-checks and pytest pass. Fix: in the <= _EPS branch, treat 'multiple answer groups but negligible spread' as discriminates=False with score 0.0 (same as a genuinely uniform question) rather than assuming a single group; or have reweight reject weights below some epsilon. Found during the 2026-08-30 vetting pass over the c5b.3.4 work.
acceptance_criteria: A self-check case in question_selector.py that builds a board with a near-zero-but-positive minority weight and asserts select_question() returns a SelectionLog (not a raise); the fix keeps the existing self-check green.
close_reason: score_candidate() now branches structurally on len(groups)==1 before the single-answer unpack, so a multi-group/negligible-spread board returns a SelectionLog instead of ValueError: too many values to unpack. Crash confirmed against the pre-fix version (HEAD:question_selector.py) and gone after. The adversarial sweep also showed the original _EPS gate was doing two unrelated jobs -- guarding float noise and deciding what is worth asking -- and set the second by accident: for a two-way split Gini is ~2x the minority fraction, so spread > 1e-9 rejected only a minority mass below ~5e-10, ~9 orders of magnitude narrower than the state the branch's own message described, with the 1e-9 boundary flipping on rounding. Replaced with _MIN_MINORITY_MASS = 1e-3, stated in belief units (share of live weight behind a differing answer) via a new _minority_mass() helper. Self-check covers three boards -- 1e-12 (abstain), 1e-4 (abstain, and >1e-9 so it proves the gate is not float noise), 0.05 relative (a live long shot that still wins) -- plus the uniform case keeping its own distinct reason string. All 5 mutations killed: reverting the gate to spread > 1e-9, dropping the len(groups)==1 guard, floor at 1.0, floor at 0.0, and min() for max() in _minority_mass.

title: Chekhov ledger: unresolved threads with an age counter
description: Track threads that were introduced and never resolved, with the turn count since each appeared. Two uses: as a writing tool it flags guns on the wall that never fire, and as chat policy it drives pacing, since long conversations lose coherence from lack of pressure rather than lack of context. Threads are either paid off or explicitly retired.
acceptance_criteria: A thread introduced and dropped shows up with its age. Retirement is an explicit entry, not silence.
close_reason: Chekhov ledger built and wired: chekhov_ledger.py (observe/use/retire/status/open_threads/retirements), integrated into chat_core.py (automatic observe/use on landed reveals, explicit retire()), and metrics.py now delegates unresolved_threads to it plus gained retired_threads()/chat_metrics()['retired']/chat_summary() line. AC met: a thread introduced and never cited shows up in open_threads() with its age; retirement is a required-reason explicit entry in retirements(), never silence. All self-checks (chekhov_ledger.py, chat_core.py, metrics.py) and full repo self-check sweep + pytest pass. Handoff at sandbox-handoffs/narrator-c5b.3.6.md.

title: Extend metrics.py to score chat transcripts
description: metrics.py already computes turn share, agreement rate and who concedes over an agent transcript. Add the chat measures: abstention rate, how often the chosen question actually split the board, and the age distribution of unresolved threads. A learner should be able to argue with these numbers.
acceptance_criteria: Runs standalone from the command line over a saved chat log and prints all three, matching the existing metrics output style.
close_reason: metrics.py now scores C5 chat logs alongside C3 debate transcripts: abstention rate, how often a chosen question was followed by the board narrowing (beside the mean predicted Gini spread of those questions), and the ages of ledger entries never used. Same JSONL loader and same CLI; the log kind is sniffed from the first row (chat rows have 'move', debate rows have 'speaker') so no flag was needed. Every rate prints beside its raw counts, since the bead asks for numbers a learner can argue with. Two definitions carry the weight: a thread is unresolved only if never cited AND never grounding anything cited -- the same recursion admissibility._grounded walks, without which an entry cited through the inference it supports reads as abandoned; and a question 'landed' only if the board shrank by the very next turn, since crediting later narrowing would credit evidence that arrived for other reasons. chat_session.jsonl is generated by running the scripted conversation through the real ChatCore and run_turn with only the model stubbed, is deterministic across runs, and the self-check regenerates and compares it so the committed copy cannot drift. Eight mutations killed: supports-not-transitive, unresolved-counts-cited, age-from-first-row, landing-window-widened, landing-direction-flipped, declined-asks-counted, abstention-counts-everything, sniff-always-true. All 16 module self-checks and pytest pass. Unblocks narrator-c5b.3.9 and narrator-c5b.3.11.

title: Chapters narrate out of chronological order
description: Root is the body at t=3 and alibi sightings are at t=2, so topological order narrates the discovery first and the earlier sightings after. Readable but not chronological. Fix means giving Root and Deduction_Culprit a t attribute and sorting the topological order by it. Found while building chapters.py.

close_reason: clue chapters now run oldest sighting first; Root stays chapter one since it is every clue's ancestor

title: load_transcript gives no context on a malformed line
description: converse() flushes one JSON object per line, so a run killed mid-write realistically leaves a truncated final line. load_transcript then raises a bare json.JSONDecodeError naming neither the file nor the line number. Found while building metrics.py.
acceptance_criteria: A malformed transcript line raises an error naming the file and the line number.
close_reason: load_transcript now enumerates lines and raises ValueError('{path}:{lineno}: {json error}') on a decode failure. ValueError is deliberate: json.JSONDecodeError already subclasses it, so nothing catching either type is affected, and metrics.py catches neither around parsing. _check_truncated_transcript covers the realistic case (a half-written object on the final line after a killed run) and asserts the reported line number is right even with a blank line earlier in the file, plus that a blank trailing line is still skipped rather than treated as corruption. agents.py, metrics.py and ocean.py self-checks all pass.

title: Culture matrix: citation sidecar before any coefficients ship
description: transform() and load_matrix() exist; the default is identity and no population coefficients are bundled. Before any matrix ships, add a sidecar source field and require it, so every coefficient set carries its citation. Invented numbers keyed to an ethnicity are stereotypes dressed as psychometrics, so unsourced matrices must not load.
acceptance_criteria: A matrix file without a source field is rejected; a sourced one loads and its citation is printed on use.
close_reason: load_matrix now requires {matrix, source}; a bare 5x5 array (the old unsourced shape) is rejected. Eight rejection cases in _check_matrix_gate: bare array, missing source, missing matrix, empty/whitespace/non-string source, wrong dimensions, non-numeric entry. A sourced matrix returns a CultureMatrix whose citation is stripped, kept, and printed to stderr by transform() on every use. The identity path still accepts a bare list so tests make no claim about any population. Default remains identity; no coefficients shipped.
